# AI Gateway Orchestrator

An asynchronous FastAPI gateway scaffold for OpenAI-compatible LLMs with exact
Redis caching, semantic caching backed by PostgreSQL/pgvector, SSE responses,
and a bounded ReAct agent runner.

## Architecture

```text
app/
├── api/v1/endpoints/       # Chat/SSE and cache management endpoints
├── core/                   # Settings, constants, and API-key authentication
├── db/                     # Async SQLAlchemy session and models
└── services/
    ├── cache/              # Redis exact cache, pgvector cache, embeddings
    ├── llm/                # OpenAI-compatible and local clients
    └── orchestrator/       # ReAct router, runner, and tools
alembic/                    # Async migrations
docker/postgres/            # pgvector initialization
tests/                      # Unit tests
```

## Quick start with Docker Compose

Requirements: Docker Desktop (or Docker Engine with Compose v2) and an
OpenAI-compatible LLM server reachable from the Docker host.

```powershell
Copy-Item .env.example .env
```

Edit `.env` before starting:

1. Set unique values for `API_KEY`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, and the password in
   `DATABASE_URL`. The database URL password must match `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`.
2. Configure `LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_MODEL`, and `LLM_API_KEY` for your model
   server. For LM Studio on the host, use
   `http://host.docker.internal:1234/v1`. For Ollama's OpenAI-compatible API,
   use `http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1`.
3. Keep `CODE_EXECUTION_ENABLED=false` unless the Docker sandbox has been
   deliberately configured and reviewed.

Start the API, PostgreSQL/pgvector, Redis, and the one-shot migration service:

```powershell
docker compose up --build -d
docker compose ps
docker compose logs --tail 100 app migrate
```

Check application health at <http://localhost:8000/health> and interactive API
documentation at <http://localhost:8000/docs>.

Stop the services with `docker compose down`. Persistent database and Redis
volumes are retained;
